question: What predicts that a partner perceives the division of household labour as fair? Cover equity theory, the distributive justice framework (outcomes, comparison referents, justifications), egocentric over-claiming of one's own contribution, and whether perceived fairness or the actual split better predicts relationship satisfaction. Report how perceived fairness has been measured.
decision_served: What a method for allocating chores between two cohabiting partners must measure, target and include so that each partner perceives the allocation as fair; feeds the burden and fairness model and the participation protocol of the methodology spec.
pico: P: adult partners in cohabiting or married couples (two-partner households) who share chores. I/E: the actual allocation of household labour (time, count, task type, cognitive labour), comparison referents, entitlement and justifications, each partner's egocentric over-claiming of their own contribution. C: equal versus unequal splits; fair-feeling versus unfair-feeling allocations; self-report versus partner or diary report of contribution. O: each partner's perceived fairness of the allocation; relationship satisfaction (marital quality, conflict, instability); how perceived fairness has been measured.

Europe PMC indexes almost no sociology of the family (Q1 returned only off-topic reviews), so OpenAlex and Crossref carried the search; Mikula 1998, Major 1993, Wilkie 1998 and Lennon 1994 were not returned by any topic query (sentinels missed).
No meta-analysis of perceived fairness of household labour and relationship satisfaction was found in two searches (Q16, Q17).

Mikula 1998, Ross & Sicoly 1979 and Kamo 2000 have no abstract in OpenAlex, Crossref or Semantic Scholar, so no abstract note could be written for them; Wilkie 1998 has only a citation line as its stored abstract.

Not requested this pass for want of request slots (papers_per_request 10): Coltrane 2000 (review, C7/C8), Kamo 2000 (C6), Petts 2025 (C7), Greenstein 1996, Grote 2002, Thompson 1991, Hawkins 1995, Major 1993, Lennon 1994 (sentinels, C2/C3/C7).
Blair & Johnson 1992 was added in pass 2 by title lookup (cited by Shelton & John 1996, Mikula 1998 and Gager 1998 as the source for task-type findings on C7); Crossref holds no abstract for it.

Pass 3: Hawkins 1995 and Lennon & Rosenfield 1994 are read from a vision model's reading of a scan (version unknown-ocr); their 38 extracts are machine-read and carry no conclusion. Hawkins's path coefficients for the split are in figures the OCR text does not carry; Lennon & Rosenfield's table-row quotes were padded to whole tokens. Check both by eye. Gager 1998 and Press & Townsley 1998 (pass 2) also stay machine-read.

Pass 3: Grote 2002's text layer drops minus signs and comparison symbols, so its Table 3 and 4 coefficients are unsigned; directions come from the authors' prose. Figure 1's path coefficients were not viewed.

Pass 3: Urbina 2025's online appendix (OSF osf.io/dwj6q, Tables A1-A4, Figure A2) is not in the text and was not read. Mikula 2009's Table 1 column labelling (m/w) is ambiguous, so its implied sums of own shares (88% and 101%) are uncertain.

Pass 3: no abstract note could be written for Grote & Clark 1998, Mederer 1993 or DeMaris & Longmore 1996 (no abstract, or only a citation line, in any index); they are requested on title and citation evidence alone. Sanchez 1994 E9 was replaced on escalation and no extract still fails.

Pass 3: no fetch route (Unpaywall, OpenAlex) offered any requested paper (Thompson 1991, Mederer 1993, DeMaris & Longmore 1996, Grote & Clark 1998, Major 1993, Braun 2008, Greenstein 1996). Not requested: Petts 2025 and Carlson 2022 (outcome is relationship satisfaction, not perceived fairness), Smith, Gager & Morgan 1998 and Grote & Clark 2001 (cited by the pass-3 papers for C8 and C4/C5; not yet in the ledger). Pass 4 is the last, so those would need to be added then.

Pass 4 (last): the seven requested papers were read (Thompson 1991, Major 1993, Greenstein 1996, Braun 2008, Grote & Clark 1998, DeMaris & Longmore 1996, Mederer 1993); six are scans, and every extract from them that carries was matched by two machine readings. Smith, Gager & Morgan 1998 and Grote & Clark 2001 were cited for C8 and C4/C5 and never entered the ledger.
